2026-09-16T14:40:45  NOTE   prerequisite-count vs pass@1 analysis on the 40-rollout run. Group means fall monotonically: 1 prereq (5 tasks, 20 rollouts) 0.400; 2 prereq (2 tasks, 8 rollouts) 0.250; 3 prereq (3 tasks, 12 rollouts) 0.167. Pearson r = -0.354, Spearman = -0.295, t(8) = -1.071, permutation p = 0.313 over 200k shuffles. The direction matches the design intent but is NOT distinguishable from noise at n=10 tasks.
2026-09-16T14:40:45  NOTE   the decisive point against reading it as a real effect: the spread WITHIN one prerequisite count exceeds the spread BETWEEN counts. At 1 prereq the five tasks score 0.75/0.75/0.50/0.00/0.00, a range of 0.75, while the whole between-group range is 0.400-0.167 = 0.233. Two single-prerequisite tasks (cd/0, savings/1) score 0.00, the same as the worst three-prerequisite task. So prerequisite count is not what is driving failure here.
2026-09-16T14:40:45  NOTE   structural caveat: in this scenario computations == prereq_count + 1 for ALL TEN tasks, exactly (one computation per problem plus the root). prereq count, computation count and resolution-order length are therefore the SAME variable by construction and cannot be separated by this data. Their correlations with pass@1 are identical (-0.354) for that reason, not because three independent signals agree. Gold-step count is only weakly collinear (12..17) and correlates -0.277.
